I farm here in Tigray and this small sorghum plot is one of several I work. With some schooling I know the value of fertilizer, but sorghum doesn't need as much as teff or wheat, and cash is tight — so I will buy a small amount of DAP from the cooperative and apply it modestly. I always spread manure from my animals on this plot before plowing, and I plant the local sorghum seed I saved from last harvest because the improved varieties are hard to find here and I trust what grows well in our soil. The rains here can be unreliable, so I won't waste money on pesticide, and there is no irrigation scheme nearby. My wife and I will do most of the work with the oxen, but I'll bring in a few neighbors to help during harvest.
